newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arafat marks week of PLO rule in Hebron.
newsitem.headline: Arafat marks week of PLO rule in Hebron.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat marked one week since Israel's handover of most of the West Bank town of Hebron to PLO-rule by dedicating a monument to the city's "liberation".

"This monument symbolizes the liberation of the city of Hebron by brother Abu Ammar (Arafat)," Hebron Mayor Mustafa Natsheh told Reuters after Arafat pressed a button to light an eternal flame on the statue of a hand holding a torch.
"It symbolizes the Palestinian resistance through the years of (Israeli) occupation and the achievement of the Palestinian dream in liberating the city," Natsheh said.
Israeli troops withdrew from 80 percent of Hebron on January 17 after months of acrimonious talks between the sides.
The town was captured by Israel in the 1967 Middle East war.

Israel remains in control of the heart of Hebron where 400 Jewish settlers live in small enclaves. Some 20,000 of Hebron's 100,000 Palestinians also live in the part of town still controlled by Israeli troops.

Hebron -- site of the Tomb of the Patriarchs which is revered by Jews and Moslems as the traditional burial place of their mutual forefather Abraham -- has long been a flashpoint of Arab-Jewish violence.

Friday, by the Moslem calendar, marked three years since Jewish settler Baruch Goldstein massacred 29 Palestinians praying at the tomb, known to Moslems as the al-Ibrahimi Mosque. Moslem prayers passed without incident on Friday.
Arafat, on his second visit to the city since its handover, was to chair a meeting of the Palestinian Authority cabinet in Hebron later in the day.
